To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the leaf litter in the tropical forest studied contains many species, that the leaf litter reflects the structure of the forest, that the leaf shadows in the litter reflect the structure of the canopy, and that the leaf litter can be a valuable source of information on the paleoenvironment.

1) the leaf litter from a high-diversity, angiosperm tropical forest is dominated by species that are rare in the forest, and 2) the litter is a biased representation of the forest canopy, with epiphytes, lianas, and vines contributing a disproportionately large number of species.

the leaf litter from a 1-ha area of undisturbed forest in southeast Peru contains 175 species of angiosperms, of which 52 species are represented in the leaf litter; that the species richness of leaf litter is a function of the richness of the canopy forest; that leaf litter is dominated by species that produce relatively small leaves; and that leaf litter contains a high proportion of epiphytes, lianas, and vines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the leaf litter approach to the reconstruction of ancient angiosperm communities.
the application of modern leaf litter data to the reconstruction of ancient high-richness forests.
the study of modern leaf litter as a tool to understand past plant communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of modern leaf litter from tropical forests provides a powerful tool for reconstructing past angiosperm communities.
tropical leaf litter is a useful tool for reconstructing the structure and dynamics of high-richness, angiosperm communities.
leaf litter studies are not yet sufficiently developed to be of use to paleobotanists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tropical forests are not just a single community but are composed of a mosaic of communities, each with its own unique characteristics.

the leaf litter of tropical forests, because of its extreme heterogeneity, provides a powerful tool for reconstructing community structure and individual species characteristics from fossil assemblages.

the modern tropical litter samples, when viewed as a proxy for the forest, provide a means for reconstructing the canopy structure of ancient forests and the species richness of the source forest, and they provide a means for studying the evolution of the tropical forest biome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leaf litter of a tropical forest is an excellent source of information about the structure of the canopy and the species composition of the forest.
the study of leaf litter in modern forests provides an important tool for paleobotanists to better understand the structure and function of ancient forests.
the leaf litter provides a unique window into the structure and dynamics of the forest community.
